theme: Alternative-data vendor sample repos: vendors publishing free samples on GitHub (Advan, Similarweb, Apptopia, Yipit-like, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, Quiver Quant, Thinknum)
queries_run: gh search repos "alternative data sample" --sort stars
gh search repos "sensor tower app rankings" --sort stars
gh search repos "consumer edge data" --sort stars
gh search repos "app store ranking history dataset" --sort stars

candidates.name: QuantConnect/Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuant
candidates.what_it_holds: QuantConnect Lean integration/example implementation pulling Quiver Quantitative's alternative-data feed (congress trading, insider trading, gov contracts, lobbying, WallStreetBets sentiment, dark-pool short volume, 13F) through their paid data marketplace. No data files committed; requires a QuiverQuant/QuantConnect subscription to pull anything.
candidates.why_useful: Quiver's actual datasets (Congress trading, WSB sentiment, Wikipedia pageviews) are not travel-demand series and don't map to a numbered gap directly, though the Wikipedia-pageviews sibling repo (Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantWikipedia) is a possible ABNB-pageviews engagement proxy (gap 5) if the API were free, which it is not for bulk history.

candidates.name: QuantConnect/Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantWikipedia
candidates.what_it_holds: Example implementation pulling QuiverQuant's Wikipedia pageview dataset (per-ticker Wikipedia page pageviews) via QuantConnect's paid data marketplace. No historical CSV committed.
candidates.why_useful: Wikipedia pageviews for the ABNB article could be an engagement/awareness proxy (gap 5); however this repo is only a connector to a paid feed, not a free source — Wikipedia's own pageviews API (wikimedia REST API) is free and better suited, and this repo is not that.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/quiver
candidates.what_it_holds: API Evangelist's third-party documentation/profile of the Quiver Quantitative API surface (endpoints for congress trading, insider trading, gov contracts, lobbying, WSB, etc.) — descriptive markdown, not a client or data.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a map of what QuiverQuant's paid API exposes; none of the covered datasets (congressional trading, lobbying, WSB sentiment) touch travel demand or STR supply directly.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/thinknum
candidates.what_it_holds: API Evangelist's independent write-up of Thinknum's alternative-data platform surface: job listings, store locations, product pricing, web traffic, app reviews, social engagement metrics tracked across companies. Descriptive markdown only, no data or working client.
candidates.why_useful: Thinknum tracks exactly the kind of company-level web/app/job-posting metrics relevant to gaps 5 (engagement, app rankings) and 15 (job-posting trackers as headcount proxy for Airbnb) — worth knowing the product exists, but this repo has zero committed data and the real Thinknum product is paid/enterprise.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/apptopia
candidates.what_it_holds: API Evangelist profile describing Apptopia's app-market-intelligence product: app download/revenue/usage/ratings/SDK-adoption estimates across iOS App Store, Google Play, Tencent, Xiaomi, Mobile 360 stores. Markdown description only, no data, no working client, no free tier documented.
candidates.why_useful: Apptopia-style app download/usage estimates for the Airbnb app would directly address gap 5 (engagement: app downloads/rankings history), but this repo is descriptive only — it confirms the product exists and roughly what it covers, nothing pullable.

candidates.name: danwagnerco/similarweb
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the official SimilarWeb API (traffic/engagement endpoints: visits, page views, bounce rate, traffic sources, by domain). No data committed; every call requires a paid SimilarWeb API key (free trial only, rate-limited).
candidates.why_useful: SimilarWeb-style web-traffic estimates for airbnb.com are named explicitly in gap 5 as a target category; this is the best-maintained (51-star, MIT) open client for that API, useful IF the team ever obtains a SimilarWeb trial key, but yields nothing without one.

candidates.name: pirsquare/SimilarWeb-Python
candidates.what_it_holds: Alternative Python client for the SimilarWeb API (traffic, referrals, apps). No committed data; requires a paid key.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as danwagnerco/similarweb (gap 5), included for redundancy/fallback in case one client is unmaintained against current API changes.

candidates.name: chat-data-llc/shopify_store_traffic_api
candidates.what_it_holds: Script using an unofficial/reverse-engineered SimilarWeb endpoint to pull traffic estimates for Shopify stores specifically (no general-domain support out of the box), no data committed, 61 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a free/unofficial SimilarWeb scrape path (no paid key) but is scoped to Shopify storefronts, not applicable to airbnb.com without rewriting; flagged only as a proof that an unofficial-endpoint route exists.

candidates.name: jsconiers/quiver-quant-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the Quiver Quantitative API — 16 tools covering congressional/insider trades, gov contracts, lobbying, WallStreetBets, dark-pool short volume, 13F. Requires a paid QuiverQuant API key; no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: 13F/insider-trade tooling touches gap 15 (company-structure signals: 13F holdings parsers) but is a generic multi-ticker wrapper, not Airbnb-specific, and needs a paid key.

candidates.name: parithosh/quiverfeed
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python library to interact with Quiver Quantitative datasets for analysis. No data committed; needs a paid API key for most endpoints (WSB sentiment has historically had a limited free tier).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — same limitation as other QuiverQuant wrappers; WallStreetBets mention-count/sentiment for ABNB could theoretically be a retail-sentiment proxy but is speculative and not in any numbered gap.

notes: This theme was a dead end for FREE sample data specifically. Advan, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, and Yipit have essentially no public GitHub footprint — zero results for 'consumer edge data', and general 'alternative data sample' also returned nothing. Apptopia and Thinknum only surfaced as API Evangelist descriptive write-ups (no client, no data, no free tier documented) plus unrelated name-collision repos (a Traditional-Chinese AI-assistant repo literally named 'Apptopia', personal test-task repos). SimilarWeb has real, maintained open-source API clients (danwagnerco/similarweb, pirsquare/SimilarWeb-Python) but all require a paid/trial API key and none carry committed historical data — they are 'method' entries only, and their practical value depends on the team getting a free-trial SimilarWeb key before 2 Oct. QuiverQuant has the most GitHub activity of any name in this list (QuantConnect Lean data-source connectors, several MCP servers, a docs profile) but its actual datasets (congress trading, insider trading, lobbying, WallStreetBets sentiment, dark-pool short volume, 13F, Wikipedia pageviews) are financial/political alt-data, not travel-demand or STR-supply data — only the Wikipedia-pageviews and 13F angles touch numbered gaps (5, 15) and even those require a paid feed through this vendor. Ran out of the 6-call gh search budget before trying 'earnest research', 'm science data', 'yipit data', 'advan research', or 'app store review scraper' / 'tranco list' / 'wikipedia pageviews api' (free, no-key alternatives to Apptopia/Similarweb for gap 5) — a follow-up scout on this theme should hit those terms first, and should also try `gh search topics` with topic=alternative-data and topic=web-scraping filtered by description keywords, since plain keyword search on vendor names mostly surfaces generic API-wrapper boilerplate and name collisions rather than data. Recommend a future scout specifically target free, no-key substitutes for these vendors: Wikimedia REST pageviews API (official, free, no key, has an existing OSS client ecosystem), Tranco top-1M list (github.com/DistrictDataLabs or tranco-list.eu client repos), Cloudflare Radar API clients (free tier), and Google Play Store review-scraper repos (google-play-scraper npm/PyPI has a GitHub source repo) as more promising routes into gap 5 than the named vendors in this theme.
